title: Adaptive KV fanout: connection-pool autosizing, graded circuit-breakers, and probabilistic load-shedding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement an adaptive strategy for downstream KV-style dependencies (Redis/managed memcache) and durable stores (Postgres/Kafka) to maintain user-visible SLOs under region partial-failures and load spikes. This ticket covers autosizing connection pools, graded circuit-breakers per dependency and per-route, and a probabilistic load-shedding layer that enables graceful, measurable degradation rather than hard failures.
background: Recent incidents showed tail latency spikes when KV fanout increased under bursty workloads and when cross-region replication lagged. Existing pool settings are static and single-threshold breakers cause synchronized failures across hosts. We need a more nuanced approach to preserve core inference SLOs while minimizing error surface area and customer-visible impact.
goals: 1) Keep customer-facing p95 request latency within SLO during downstream stress for at least 90% of incidents. 2) Avoid system-wide failure cascades by localizing degradation and isolating noisy callers. 3) Provide clear metrics and runbook steps to restore full functionality.
non_goals: Prevent every single cache miss from impacting latency; replace long-term sharding/DB re-architecture; implement new persistence replication protocols.
proposal_options: Option A: Conservative - global static pool sizes + single threshold circuit-breaker. Fast to ship but brittle under multi-region skew.

Option B: Reactive - per-region dynamic pool autosizing driven by observed request concurrency and latency heatmaps. Two-tier circuit-breakers (soft then hard) and request scoring for probabilistic shedding.
Option C: Aggressive - route-level sharding + per-caller quotas, constant-rate shedding at ingress. Highest isolation but highest engineering cost.
decision: Adopt Option B. Implement per-region adaptive connection pools sized by a conservative formula (pool = max(10, ceil(average_concurrency * headroom_factor))). Use two-stage, graded circuit-breakers: a soft breaker that starts shedding low-priority traffic probabilistically when 95th latency exceeds soft_threshold (200ms for KV reads), and a hard breaker that trips on sustained error rate or consecutive timeouts (error_rate > 5% over 60s OR 50 consecutive timeouts) and drops non-essential fanout for the duration. Integrate a token-based admission control to bound queue growth and return 429/Retry-After for excess requests. Expose per-route and per-dependency metrics and configure automatic rollback to normal operation once health signals recover for 120s.
acceptance_criteria: Can simulate region partial-failure in staging and show degraded but healthy behavior: core requests meet p95 SLO in 90% of runs.
No cascading connection exhaustion across pods when fanout multiplier doubles in a region for 10 minutes.
Circuit-breaker metrics (state transitions, shed_count) surface in console and trigger alerts when thresholds exceeded.
Runbook steps documented and validated in war-game with oncall; linked PRs and dashboards available.
metrics: User-visible SLO: request p95 latency < 250ms for text-gen read paths under normal load (target).
Staged SLO under KV stress: p95 latency < 400ms for core paths with <= 10% shedding allowed for non-core endpoints.
Breaker thresholds: soft_threshold=200ms (95th), hard_error_rate=5% (60s window), consecutive_timeouts=50.
Pool health metrics: pool_size, inbound_queue_length, connection_wait_ms, connections_opened_per_minute.
Recovery metrics: time_to_closed (breaker), time_to_recover (health sustained for 120s).
runbook: Pager triggers on: hard breaker open in >3 pods in region OR shed_rate > 20% for >5m.

Immediate actions: 1) Scale dedicated pool nodeset for affected region (runtime-ops). 2) Swap to read-only fallback for non-critical routes. 3) If storage replication lag detected, re-route reads to nearest healthy replica using cross-region TTL logic.
Post-incident: collect profiles, attach slow RPC traces, run traffic replay to staging for validation before changing thresholds.
